subject: Surge protection SLA: surge credits, pricing, and packaging options
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Avery Cole <avery@sundrycloud.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 27 Aug 2025 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Surge protection SLA: surge credits, pricing, and packaging options

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the time yesterday — good context on the seasonal burst patterns you see in Q4. Per our conversation I attached a first-pass SKU sheet that models two approaches for handling unexpected traffic surges:

- Surge Protection Add-on (per-month): keeps a reserved headroom that buys you a higher uptime SLA for peak windows and immediate priority routing.
- On-demand Surge Credits: credits consumed during peak bursts; cheaper baseline but no guaranteed immediate capacity.

Key asks so we can tailor pricing:
1) Typical P95 token throughput during peak bursts (per-region).
2) Expected max burst duration (minutes/hours).
3) Whether you need guaranteed regional failover or cross-region acceptable.

Attachment: surge-protection-sku.xlsx (xlsx, 1 sheet)

If you like, I can put together a blended quote that shows cost delta for the next 12 months (with and without the introductory discount we discussed).

Thanks,
—Naomi

Avery —

Quick answers below and inline with the SKU file:

- Response times: Priority-1 (service-impairing) will have a 15-minute acknowledgement SLO and 2-hour remediation target when Surge Protection Add-on is active. For On-demand Surge Credits, acknowledgement is 30 minutes and remediation target is 4 hours. We recommend Add-on for customers who need guaranteed fastfallover.

- Credit model: credits are token-based (credits per 1M tokens) and are consumed only during declared surge windows or when traffic exceeds your baseline + buffer. The SKU sheet includes an example calculation for a 3x spike.

- Pilot band pricing: attached is a blended quote for a 12-month pilot at ~500M tokens/month baseline with a 3x spike allowance. The blended quote shows list price and an introductory 10% pilot discount.

Attachment: mexp-draft-terms.pdf (pdf)

If procurement needs a simpler redlineable T&C, we can push a PO-friendly exhibit that converts the Add-on into a monthly SKU and appends the surge-credit accounting table.

Best,
—Naomi

Saw the pilot pricing Naomi put together. A couple of operational notes from the finance/offer side:

- If we offer a 10% pilot discount we should limit it to the first 12 months and require a minimum 6-month committed seat to avoid churn exposure.
- Margin impact for the Add-on is higher (because of reserved capacity), recommend we gate the Add-on by a minimum committed spend of $75k/month for Enterprise customers. For smaller pilots we should steer them to On-demand Surge Credits.

If Laura is OK with the gating language I can incorporate the tiered pricing into the HubSpot quote and produce a PO-ready line item.

Maya / Avery —

Thanks for the redlines. Summary of agreed changes and next steps:

- Acknowledgement measurement: OK to start the SLA clock from the shared triage channel timestamp; we'll add a definitional exhibit to the SOW.
- Remediation target: we will accept a "best-effort" 2-hour remediation target for the pilot but will maintain a 2-hour contractual remediation target for Add-on customers after pilot conversion.
- Service credit cap: we can accept the 20% monthly invoice cap for the pilot only. For longer-term Add-on commitments the cap will revert to our standard 10% (to protect capacity economics).
- Failover testing: we can schedule an initial simulated failover test during onboarding; operations will coordinate a 4-hour window.

I've updated the pilot quote, limited the 10% introductory discount to months 1–12, and added the minimum $75k/month gate for converting to Add-on. I've attached the PO-friendly exhibit and included a DocuSign link for the redlined SOW.
